slides.title: Returns cost us more than shipping does
slides.subtitle: What we found in six months of returns data, and the one change we propose

slides.title: One in five orders comes back, and each return costs twice the outbound trip
slides.body: Fixing sizing on three product lines would remove most of that cost.
slides.notes: Open with the cost comparison. The audience thinks shipping is the big line item; it is not.

slides.title: Returns now cost more than outbound shipping
slides.label: spent handling returns in the first half of 2026
slides.context: Outbound shipping cost $0.7m over the same months.

slides.title: Return rates doubled after the March size-chart change
bullets: March is when the new size chart went live
slides.notes: The step change lines up with the size chart release on 4 March.

slides.title: Three product lines account for most returned units
slides.source: Warehouse system, returned units January to June 2026
slides.notes: The top three lines are all sized garments with the new chart.

slides.title: Fixing sizing on the top three lines saves about $0.6m a year
slides.notes: Each bar is the saving if that line's return rate goes back to its January level.

slides.title: Wrong size is the reason given for most returns
slides.notes: Too small is the single biggest reason and it grew the most.

slides.title: Customers who returned for size still liked the product
slides.notes: This is a sizing problem, not a product problem.

slides.title: Customers tell us the chart runs small
slides.quote: I am always a medium, but your medium was tight across the shoulders.
slides.notes: Many comments say the same thing in different words.
